transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm in the right place for this. I guess... what finally made me come in is that I'm just having a little trouble keeping up with, like, basic adult things? I mean, I'm sure everyone struggles a bit right out of college, right? 

But I keep, um... I keep forgetting things. Like paying my bills, or... returning emails for job interviews. And showing up for appointments or just following through on regular errands. I really don't mean to be careless, I promise, I just... it completely slips my mind. I'm a little embarrassed to even admit it, but it's actually started costing me some real opportunities lately. I just really want to fix it so I can be more reliable. Is that... does that make sense as a reason to be here?

Can you tell me if these difficulties with forgetfulness and following through on tasks have been happening mostly when you’re feeling down or low in mood, or do they seem to happen even when you’re feeling okay?

Oh, um... no, I don't think it's tied to feeling down. I mean, I actually feel pretty good most days! I try to be a really positive person. 

But... even when I'm having a great week and feeling totally fine, I still just, you know, completely drop the ball on things. I hope that doesn't make me sound worse? Like, I know it means I don't really have a good excuse for messing up... but yeah, it happens even when I'm completely happy. Is that... does that answer your question okay?
Can you tell me if these tasks you forget or don’t complete tend to be things you find boring or uninteresting, or if they’re things you genuinely care about and want to do?

Um, well... I guess I'd say it's a mix of both? I mean, I definitely struggle more with the boring stuff, like paperwork or organizing my room. I think anyone would rather avoid that, right? 

But... honestly, and this is the part I feel really bad about... I forget the things I actually care about, too. Like, I'll be so excited about a potential job, and I genuinely want it, but I'll still forget to send the follow-up email. Or I'll make plans with a friend I really want to see, and then completely lose track of time and show up an hour late, or forget entirely until they text me. 

I really, really don't want people to think I don't care, because I do! I care so much. It just... it just happens anyway. I'm sorry, I know that probably sounds terrible. Am I making sense?
Can you tell me if you have trouble staying focused on one thing for a while, like reading a book or listening during a conversation, or if your mind tends to jump around a lot?

Um, yeah, I guess my mind does jump around a bit. I mean, I'm sure everyone gets a little distracted sometimes, right? It's so normal with all the technology we have now. 

But... well, I guess it does happen to me a lot. Like, I'll sit down with the best intentions to update my resume or, um, work on a coding practice problem, and... I don't know, a text notification will pop up, or I'll hear someone talking outside, or even just... a random thought about something else I need to do will pop into my head. And before I even realize what happened, I'm completely off track. 

I really try to stay focused, I promise. It's just... it's like my brain just takes a detour without asking me first. I hope that doesn't make me sound flighty or anything. I really do try to pay attention. Is that... is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
Can you tell me if these difficulties with forgetfulness and getting distracted started early in your life, like when you were a child, or if they seem to have developed more recently as an adult?

Um, well... I think it's been going on for a really long time. Like, since I was a kid. I mean, I know most kids are a little disorganized and energetic, right? That's just a normal part of growing up. 

But... well, looking back at my old elementary school report cards, it was definitely happening back then, too. The teachers were always really sweet, they always made a point to write that I was bright! Which I was so grateful for. But... then they would also usually add that I constantly lost my worksheets. And that I'd rush through directions without really reading them. 

I also... well, I had a habit of talking out of turn a lot. I really didn't mean to be a disruptive kid, I promise! I just got so eager to participate and the words would just fall out. And my desk... it was always so messy that I could never find my assignments when it was time to hand them in. 

I always felt so bad about it, because I really did want to be a good student for them and do things right. Does that... does that make sense? Is that the kind of timeline you were looking for?
